sentences.text:
Miscellaneous Second Appeal No. 86 of 2025
 Mukesh Singh Kirar
 Versus
The State Of Madhya Pradesh

Appearance:
 Shri Anil Kumar Sharma - Advocate for appellant.
 Shri S.S. Kushwaha - Govt. Advocate for respondent/State.
Judgment

This miscellaneous second appeal under Section 71 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 has been filed against the judgment dated 14/08/2025 passed by Principal District Judge, Gwalior /
Appellate Authority under the Food Safety and Standards Act, in R.C.A No. 90/2025, as well as order dated 09/12/2024 passed by the Additional District Magistrate / Adjudicating Officer in Case No. Q/Food Safety/112/2023.
2.
The facts necessary for disposal of present appeal, in short, are that firm of the appellant was inspected by the Food Safety Officer on 12/03/2023 at 11:00 a.m.
On inspection, it was found that 25 kg of Paneer was kept in a freezer, 60 litres of milk was kept in a container, and 25 kg of butter was kept in a drum.
They were stored for sale for human consumption.
Since the Food Safety Officer had suspicion about the quality of food articles, therefore, samples were collected and they were sent to the Food Analyst.
The Food Analyst, by his report dated 12/06/2023, informed that the 2 MSA-86-2025 Paneer was of substandard quality.
A copy of report of the Food Analyst was sent to the appellant with information that he can prefer an appeal, if he so desires, under Section 46(4) of the Food Safety and Standards Act.
Appellant made an endorsement that he does not want retesting of the food article from the referral laboratory.
Accordingly, the complaint was filed.

3. The Adjudicating Officer, by order dated 09/12/2024, held the appellant guilty of violation of Sections 51 and 58 of the Food Safety and Standards Act and imposed a penalty of Rs. 1,00,000/-
for violation of Section 51 and Rs. 30,000/- for violation of Section 58 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, and in all imposed a final penalty of Rs. 1,30,000/-.

sentences.text: Being aggrieved by the order passed by Adjudicating Officer, appellant preferred an appeal, which has been dismissed by the Appellate Authority.
5. Challenging the orders passed by Authorities below, it is submitted by counsel for appellant that appellant is a petty trader and penalty of Rs. 1,30,000/- is on a higher side.
Penalty should be such that a wrongdoer may not be required to face adverse circumstances.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for State supported the orders passed by Authorities below.

7. Heard learned counsel for parties.
8.
Policy of sentencing is based on the principle of deterrence.
Therefore, counsel for appellant is wrong in submitting that penalty should not be such which may cause undue hardship to the wrongdoer.
9. The Paneer, which was kept by appellant for sale for human 3 MSA-86-2025 consumption, was found to be of substandard quality.
It is not the case of appellant that he had already displayed in his shop/firm that substandard Paneers are being sold.
On the contrary, it is clear that appellant was selling t h e Paneer by claiming that it is pure, and thereby, had also defrauded innocent consumers.
How the sale of substandard quality of eatables can be dealt with in a lenient manner could not be explained by counsel for appellant.

10. Under these circumstances, specifically when appellant had given in writing that he does not wish a retesting by the referral laboratory, and Paneer was found to be of substandard quality and 25 kg of Paneer was stored by appellant in his shop, this Court is of considered opinion that no case is made out warranting interference.

11. Accordingly, judgment dated 14/08/2025 passed by Principal District Judge, Gwalior / Appellate Authority under the Food Safety and Standards Act, in R.C.A No. 90/2025, as well as order dated 09/12/2024 passed by the Additional District Magistrate / Adjudicating Officer in Case No. Q/Food Safety/112/2023 are hereby affirmed.

entities.text: Principal District Judge, Gwalior / Appellate Authority
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 12. The appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.
